physics-killer-06.title: On a frictionless horizontal
physics-killer-06.goal: Apply principles to solve the inquiry problem.
physics-killer-06.material: On a frictionless horizontal surface, object A of mass $2\,\mathrm{kg}$ moves at $6\,\mathrm{m/s}$ and collides with object B of mass $4\,\mathrm{kg}$ at rest; the two objects stick together and move as one. If the collision lasts $0.05\,\mathrm{s}$, which option correctly gives, in order, the speed of the two objects just after the collision and the magnitude of the average force on B during the collision?
physics-killer-06.s.s1.prompt: On a frictionless horizontal surface, object A of mass $2\,\mathrm{kg}$ moves at $6\,\mathrm{m/s}$ and collides with object B of mass $4\,\mathrm{kg}$ at rest; the two objects stick together and move as one. If the collision lasts $0.05\,\mathrm{s}$, which option correctly gives, in order, the speed of the two objects just after the collision and the magnitude of the average force on B during the collision?
physics-killer-06.s.s1.explain: Momentum conservation: $2\cdot6=(2+4)v\Rightarrow v=2\,\mathrm{m/s}$. The change in B's momentum is $\Delta p_B=4\cdot2-0=8\,\mathrm{kg\cdot m/s}$, so $F_{avg}=\dfrac{8}{0.05}=160\,\mathrm{N}$. (A's momentum change $2(2-6)=-8$ has the same magnitude, consistent.) Using only $m_A$ in the denominator gives $v=3\,\mathrm{m/s}$ (option 1); using A's initial momentum $12$ in the force calculation gives $240\,\mathrm{N}$ (option 2); applying the elastic-collision $v_B=4\,\mathrm{m/s}$ gives option 3.
physics-killer-06.s.s2.prompt: Which scenario demonstrates the correct real-world application of this principle?
physics-killer-06.s.s2.explain: The fundamental principles of this inquiry are widely implemented in modern technology.
